findings.title: No WAF / CDN fingerprints detected
findings.evidence: Headers, cookies, and a tripwire request did not match known WAF signatures.
findings.remediation: If you expect a WAF in front of this site, verify it's actually serving traffic for this hostname.

findings.title: WordPress core is up to date (7.1)
findings.evidence: Detected 7.1 via meta generator tag on /; latest is 7.0.
findings.remediation: No action needed.

findings.title: 1 plugin(s) discovered via HTML asset paths
findings.evidence:
Plugin slugs found across 5 probed page(s):
  - gutenberg  (version: 23.2.2)
findings.remediation: Plugin slugs being discoverable is normal but useful to attackers. Keep all listed plugins updated. Consider a WAF that strips ?ver= asset query strings.

findings.title: 1 plugin(s) expose readme.txt with version
findings.evidence:
readme.txt accessible for:
  - gutenberg: version 23.2.2
findings.remediation: Block /wp-content/plugins/*/readme.txt at the server level. Public readme files leak exact plugin versions, making CVE matching trivial.

findings.title: 2 theme(s) discovered via HTML asset paths
findings.evidence:
Theme slugs found:
  - wporg-parent-2021  (version: 1.0.0-6ebb648)
  - wporg-main-2022  (version: 1.0.0-4837c60)
findings.remediation: Keep all installed themes updated, including inactive ones. Delete unused themes — inactive themes still receive PHP execution if a CVE lands.

findings.title: REST users endpoint exposed via ?rest_route= query
findings.evidence: /?rest_route=/wp/v2/users returned 6 user(s).
findings.remediation: Same fix as /wp-json/wp/v2/users — filter out the users endpoint via rest_endpoints.

findings.title: Exposed: cron endpoint present at /wp-cron.php
findings.evidence:
GET /wp-cron.php → 200 (text/html; charset=utf-8)
  preview: (binary, 0 bytes)
findings.remediation: Remove /wp-cron.php from the document root immediately, or add a server-level deny rule. For backups/secrets, also rotate any credentials they contained — assume they are compromised.

findings.title: /wp-admin/ reachable
findings.evidence: GET /wp-admin/ → 302
findings.remediation: Same as wp-login.php — restrict by IP/2FA or rename the admin path.

findings.title: XML-RPC endpoint is enabled
findings.evidence: POST /xmlrpc.php system.listMethods → 200 with valid methodResponse. system.multicall + wp.getUsersBlogs available — amplification + brute-force vector.
findings.remediation: If you don't use Jetpack or the WP mobile app, disable XML-RPC. Block /xmlrpc.php at the server (Nginx: `location = /xmlrpc.php { deny all; }`). If you need it, restrict by IP and disable system.multicall via the `xmlrpc_methods` filter to neutralize the brute-force amplifier.

findings.title: Missing security header: content-security-policy
findings.evidence: GET / response did not include content-security-policy.
findings.remediation: Add a Content-Security-Policy. Start with a report-only policy to map your asset hosts, then enforce. Even a permissive `default-src 'self' https:; object-src 'none'` blocks the most common XSS payloads.

findings.title: Missing security header: x-content-type-options
findings.evidence: GET / response did not include x-content-type-options.
findings.remediation: Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` to stop MIME sniffing.

findings.title: Missing security header: referrer-policy
findings.evidence: GET / response did not include referrer-policy.
findings.remediation: Add `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.

findings.title: Missing security header: permissions-policy
findings.evidence: GET / response did not include permissions-policy.
findings.remediation: Add a `Permissions-Policy` header to disable powerful APIs (camera, microphone, geolocation, etc.) for any features you don't use.

findings.title: Server / X-Powered-By headers leak software info
findings.evidence: Server: nginx
findings.remediation: Suppress these headers. Nginx: `more_clear_headers Server X-Powered-By;` (headers-more module) or `server_tokens off;`. PHP: set `expose_php = Off` in php.ini.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header present (deep grading skipped)
findings.evidence: See the 'TLS & security headers' check for the basic header-presence finding.
findings.remediation: Adding a baseline CSP — even `default-src 'self' https:; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'` — blocks the most common XSS payloads.

findings.title: wp-emoji-release.min.js exposes WP version via ?ver= (7.1)
findings.evidence: Found `wp-emoji-release.min.js?ver=7.1` in homepage.
findings.remediation: Disable the emoji feature (it's rarely useful): `remove_action('wp_head','print_emoji_detection_script', 7);` and the related actions. Or strip ?ver= from all asset URLs via a filter.

findings.title: robots.txt advertises 1 sensitive-looking path(s)
findings.evidence:
Disallow entries that look interesting:
  - /wp-admin/
findings.remediation: robots.txt is read by everyone, including attackers. Don't list staging or admin URLs there — block them via auth or IP allow-listing instead. The Disallow only asks polite bots to stay away; it doesn't restrict access.

findings.title: No SQL injection indicators on tested parameters
findings.evidence: Probed 5 common WP parameters with error/boolean/time payloads. WP core has long been hardened against these vectors; real-world WP SQLi usually lives in plugins. This is reassuring but not exhaustive.
findings.remediation: No action needed for the tested endpoints. Keep all plugins updated and prefer plugins from reputable maintainers.

findings.title: Parameter 'author_name' is reflected (brackets escaped)
findings.evidence: Marker 'wpsx4f005b50' reflected; angle brackets appear escaped. Low risk on its own, but quote-context bugs can still enable attribute-break XSS.
findings.remediation: Ensure attribute values in PHP templates are wrapped with esc_attr().

findings.title: Parameter 'post_type' is reflected (brackets escaped)
findings.evidence: Marker 'wpsx4f005b50' reflected; angle brackets appear escaped. Low risk on its own, but quote-context bugs can still enable attribute-break XSS.
findings.remediation: Ensure attribute values in PHP templates are wrapped with esc_attr().

findings.title: Open redirect via wp-login.php?redirect_to=https://...
findings.evidence:
GET /wp-login.php with {'redirect_to': 'https://wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid/landed'} -> 301
  Location: https://login.wordpress.org/?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fwordpress.org%2F
  Target host 'login.wordpress.org' is not the scanned host 'wordpress.org'.
findings.remediation: Validate redirect targets against an allow-list, or use wp_safe_redirect() which strips off-host destinations. Open redirects are commonly chained into phishing campaigns and OAuth-token theft.

findings.title: Open redirect via wp-login.php?redirect_to=//host (protocol-relative)
findings.evidence:
GET /wp-login.php with {'redirect_to': '//wpsecscan-redirect-test.invalid'} -> 301
  Location: https://login.wordpress.org/?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fwordpress.org%2F
  Target host 'login.wordpress.org' is not the scanned host 'wordpress.org'.
findings.remediation: Validate redirect targets against an allow-list, or use wp_safe_redirect() which strips off-host destinations. Open redirects are commonly chained into phishing campaigns and OAuth-token theft.
